title: Top court refuses interim relief to Umar and Sharjeel, seeks Delhi Police response
description: Supreme Court Seeks Delhi Police's Response To The Activists' Fresh Bail Pleas But Declines Interim Relief, With Next Hearing Scheduled For December 14
author: Our Bureau
content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued a notice to Delhi Police seeking its response to separate bail applications filed by rights activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots case.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana, however, refrained from granting any interim bail and posted the matter for further hearing to December 14.
“Issue notice, returnable on December 14, 2026. The registry is directed to put up the matter before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India, on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench in light of the judgment dated May 22, 2026, passed by this court in Tasleem Ahmed Vs State of Govt of NCT of Delhi 2026,” the bench said.
Khalid and Imam cited their prolonged incarceration, delay in the examination of witnesses and the top court’s decision last January to allow them to file bail pleas after a year.
Both Khalid and Imam contended that they had been in jail for six years and nine months and over 900 witnesses were yet to be examined, which means the trial would take considerable time to conclude. Their continued incarceration as undertrials violated their fundamental right to life and liberty under Article 21, they submitted.
The duo also referred to the May 18 judgment of a bench of Justice B.V. Nagarathna and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan that another “two-judge” bench had in January violated “judicial discipline” by denying bail to Khalid and Imam.

title: CJP leader moves court over UK travel bar after being stopped from flying to Oxford
description: Saurav Das Tells Delhi HC He Was Stopped Without An Order; Centre Says Passport Office Issued A Showcause Notice Over Alleged Discrepancy In Place Of Birth
author: Our Bureau
content:
Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday approached Delhi High Court against the government’s decision to stop him from flying to the UK for an event at Oxford University.
Later in the day, the external affairs ministry said a showcause notice had been issued to Das over an alleged discrepancy regarding his place of birth in his passport.
Das, who was scheduled to speak on the “cockroach movement” at Oxford University, was stopped by the immigration authorities at Delhi airport on Monday night.
Das’s lawyer Krishnesh Bapat requested a bench of acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma to grant an urgent hearing to the petition.
“I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC (lookout circular), no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel. I am seeking listing of a fresh petition today. I can still make it to the United Kingdom on November 27, which is where my arrangements are,” Das’s petition stated.
Bapat told the court that Das could catch another flight to the UK on Thursday.
“Let it be (heard) tomorrow (Thursday),” the bench said.
External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the regional passport office in Chennai issued the showcause notice to Das on Monday, and he was asked to respond to it within seven days.
“The passport application provides for declaration of correct information by the applicant. If at any stage a discrepancy is noted, or reported by authorities, which amounts to suppression of facts, then we issue a showcause notice to the applicant to explain his or her point of view,” Jaiswal said.
He said Das was also advised not to use the passport until he submitted a response to the notice.

title: Rahul asset scan bid halted by Supreme Court, fresh hearing ordered in open court
description: Apex Court Sets Aside Allahabad HC Order For CBI And ED Verification, Directing A Fresh Bench To Rehear The PIL After Rahul Gandhi Is Impleaded
author: Our Bureau
content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside an Allahabad High Court order that had directed the CBI and the ED to verify a BJP leader’s allegation that Rahul Gandhi held assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.
A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant requested the high court to constitute a fresh bench to rehear the matter after impleading Rahul, who was not heard before the order was passed.
The bench, which also had Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana, said the matter would be heard in open court and turned down the request of petitioner and BJP leader S. Vignesh Shishir, who had sought in-camera proceedings citing apprehensions about his life and safety.
“The impugned orders passed by the high court are set aside. The matter shall be placed before the high court Chief Justice for constituting a fresh bench, which shall commence the proceedings afresh in open court,” CJI Kant said while dictating the order.
The bench also said the parties to the dispute were free to raise their contentions, including the maintainability of the PIL.
The bench was dealing with Rahul’s petition challenging the high court’s order.
Rahul had submitted that Shishir’s PIL was politically motivated and that he was not heard when the impugned orders were passed.
Rahul had also filed a separate transfer petition to shift the matter from Allahabad High Court to Delhi High Court, which the top court did not consider.

title: Saurav Das CJP: Indian government has 'lost the plot' says 'cockroach' party leader after being barred from UK flight
description: Saurav Das says immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him his passport had been flagged.
author: Rajini Vaidyanathan, Jamie Whitehead
content:
Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight
- Published
One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.
Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.
In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people.
The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.
Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared".
"They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them."
By not allowing him to travel, he said the government had lowered India's stature in the world.
"It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he said. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light.
"It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government."
Das said he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement.
Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country."
On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".
Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.
In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .
In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.
The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Das insisted the CJP would continue protesting, but it did not want to be a political party "as of today".
"It's a long haul. We are not here for a short time. We are looking at India in the next 10 to 20 years. How do we develop India into a better country? That is the vision that we want to carry forward."
Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.
There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.
In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.
In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.
Additional reporting by Cherylann Mollan.

title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: 15-year-old smashes the record for the fastest List A double century
description: India's 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blazes 204 from 53 balls for India A, almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket.
author: Mike Peter
content:
Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record by scoring 204 off 53 balls
- Published
India's 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit the most sixes ever recorded in a senior men's innings in blazing 204 from 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates.
While almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi hit 28 sixes and seven fours in the Asia Cup Rising Stars competition - easily breaking Chad Bowes' previous record of 103 balls from 2024.
The teenage opener also broke the record for the fastest century and 150, the latter of which he already held, before being caught at long-off with his side five runs from victory.
India A ultimately passed their target of 250, played against a UAE side that featured a number of internationals but was not their current first-choice side, in 14.2 overs in Doha.
Sooryavanshi now holds the following records in List A cricket, the categorisation given to senior one-day matches:
- Fastest fifty: 11 balls v Sri Lanka A, 21 June (previously Kaushalya Weeraratne, 12 balls, 1 November 2005)
- Fastest hundred: 28 balls, today (previously Jake Fraser-McGurk, 29 balls, 8 October 2023)
- Fastest 150: 40 balls, today (previously himself, 59 balls, 24 December 2025)
- Fastest 200: 52 balls, today (previously Chad Bowes, 103 balls, 22 October 2024)
The previous record for the most sixes in senior matches was 26, struck by Tanmay Agarwal in an innings of 366 for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in India's first-class Ranji Trophy competition in January 2024.
The record in List A cricket was 23 sixes, struck by D'Arcy Short for Queensland in his 257 against Tasmania on 28 September 2018.
Sooryavanshi also holds the records of being the youngest century-maker in both List A and T20 cricket and the youngest captain in T20s.
"The first thing that's required in this format is being fearless, he's got plenty of that," former India batter Deep Dasgupta told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"Technically he's quite unique. There is a tendency of being over-coached in this generation, there's so many coaches and when you start playing franchise cricket.
"The best part is he has been fast-tracked so he hasn't had a lot of coaches, he's kind of untouched. What you see of him is predominantly what his natural game is.
"That bat swing, the hand speed, which is very, very natural and one of the quickest you'll come across. Technically he's very gifted, he's very special and he's definitely the real deal."
Sooryavanshi has rapidly become a sensation in T20 cricket since making his debut in the Indian Premier League in 2025 at the age of 14.
He has hit two hundreds and six fifties in his first two seasons in the competition and has earned 10 caps for India in the shortest format since making his debut against England in July.
The left-hander, who was batting in only his 16th List A innings in Doha and made his second century in the format, is yet to play for India in 50-over cricket.
He put on partnerships of 68 with opening partner Abhishek Sharma, who scored 12, 40 with Prabhsimran Singh, who added just three, and 137 with Rinku Singh, who scored an unbeaten 27.
The India A side, which featured a number of internationals, restricted the UAE to 249-8 in 50 overs, external after their opposition had chosen to bat and swiftly reached 254-3 to win by seven wickets and guarantee their place in the semi-finals.
The Rising Stars competition features A sides from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Afghanistan alongside squads from the UAE, Nepal and Hong Kong.
India A, who now top Group B, beat Nepal and lost to Pakistan A in their previous two matches in the competition, with Sooryavanshi making scores of 26 and 11.
Pakistan A will retake the top spot if they beat Nepal on Tuesday, with semi-finals on Thursday and Friday to follow before Sunday's final.

title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah visit: India to give $1.62bn economic package
description: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.
author: Azadeh Moshiri
content:
India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
- Published
Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah has repeatedly called for his country to be treated as an equal by its powerful neighbours. His first visit to the Indian capital, Delhi, put that approach to the test, as both sides sought to reset a relationship strained by years of friction.
The contrast between the two leaders was striking.
Shah, 36, wearing his trademark black suit and sunglasses, stood beside Prime Minister Narendra Modi, 76, dressed in white. Shah rose to power after a wave of Gen Z-led protests toppled his predecessor.
Modi, meanwhile, is serving a third term and has recently faced student-led protests in India.
Yet, the two leaders seemed determined to project warmer relations. They exchanged gifts, inspected a military guard of honour and jointly flagged off a new cross-border train service.
For Nepal, the stakes were about far more than repairing diplomatic ties.
The two countries announced a series of agreements covering trade, hydropower, transport and education for Nepali youths.
India, more crucially, unveiled a $1.6bn (£1.22bn) support package as Nepal recovers from devastating floods earlier this year.
The floods killed more than 1,400 people, with thousands still missing. Shah's government has faced criticism over support for families which lost homes and loved ones.
The country faces a huge reconstruction challenge. The government estimates rebuilding could cost as much as $4.8bn. Addressing the UN General Assembly in September, Shah warned that when climate disasters devastate poorer countries, "the answer cannot simply be another mega-loan".
Modi pledged nearly $1.6bn in Indian support. Most of it will come as a line of credit for energy projects, alongside about $400m in grants for reconstruction and infrastructure.
While Nepal would have preferred a larger package, former senior Nepali diplomat Vijay Kant Karna says it is still "a significant amount" and could help stabilise a relationship that has often been uneasy.
A Hindu-majority nation wedged between India and China, Nepal has long had to navigate competing interests from its two giant neighbours. Allegations of political interference and an unresolved border dispute have frequently complicated ties with India.
Nepal's former Prime Minister, KP Sharma Oli, who leads a communist party, was widely viewed as being closer to China. Shah, by contrast, emerged as a political outsider when he was elected earlier this year. The former rapper, then 35, led a party that was only four years old.
His new approach of dealing with India may explain why the border dispute was largely absent from the leaders' public remarks, although the joint statement acknowledged that outstanding issues remained.
According to Govind Pokharel, a former vice-chairman of Nepal's National Planning Commission, Shah's government may have chosen to set contentious issues aside in order to secure progress on more immediate development needs.
"Right now you can go home and convince the young Nepalis that it will be handled later," Pokhrel says, "but if they don't deal with these issues in the future, there will be criticism."
Veteran Indian diplomat Anil Trigunayat says both sides appear to have opted to leave the dispute to established mechanisms rather than engage in what he calls "cartographic aggressions".
There were other gains for Nepal as a result of the Delhi visit.
As a landlocked country heavily dependent on India for trade, Nepal secured access to two additional Indian ports, Kandla and Paradip. The two sides also agreed to improve road and rail connectivity.
The leaders jointly inaugurated a train service linking Ayodhya in India, revered by Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Ram, with Janakpur in Nepal, traditionally regarded as the birthplace of his wife Sita.
There was, however, disappointment on aviation.
Nepal has long sought greater access to Indian airspace in order to attract international traffic to its airports at Bhairahawa and Pokhara.
Some analysts believe the lack of an agreement reflects Indian concerns over Chinese involvement in the two airport projects.
"The airport in Pokhara can pose certain security challenges for India, so it is a more complicated issue to resolve," says Trigunayat.
India did, however, agree to make an existing air route linking Kathmandu, Bhairahawa and Lucknow bidirectional.
"Nepal invested a huge amount of money in those airports," says Pokharel. "It fell short of expectations, but the bidirectional route is a breakthrough."
Shah must now manage relations with China as he seeks to balance the interests of Nepal's two much larger neighbours.
For now he returns home with substantial financial commitments from India as Nepal continues the long task of rebuilding.

title: Karnataka minister faces heat over ‘gold necklace’ remark on ASHA workers protesting for higher wages
description: Minister Narendra Swamy invoked a Kannada saying whe speaking about the protests Tuesday. Saying translates to: 'We cannot give a gold necklace every time anyone asks for anything'.
author: Sharan Poovanna
content:
Bengaluru: A minister’s remark on protesting ASHA workers has turned into a noose of sorts for the Congress government in Karnataka. Agriculture Minister P.M. Narendra Swamy’s comment made earlier this week on “not being able to give necklaces” to healthcare workers seeking higher wages has drawn sharp criticism for being what most say was “insensitive”.
Kannada actor and former parliamentarian from Mandya Ramya (Divya Spandhana) said the comments added insult to injury for ASHA workers, who have been protesting for higher wages in Bengaluru for the past nine days.
“Insensitive statement by Narendraswamy. Our ASHA sisters carried us through Covid, door to door, and they care for every mother and newborn in our villages. All they ask is a living wage. Mocking them is unacceptable. The Minister must apologise to the ASHA sisters,” Ramya posted on social media platform X.
Swamy was interacting with mediapersons in Mysuru Tuesday when he invoked a Kannada saying in response to a question about the protests. The saying translates to: “We cannot give a gold necklace every time anyone asks for anything; no government is financially that strong.” The term Swamy used for necklace was ‘kaanthi haara’, meaning gold necklace.
ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) workers are instrumental in bridging the gap between the public and the government healthcare system, especially in the hinterland. Some 15,000 workers have been protesting at Bengaluru’s freedom park in the cold and heat, demanding a wage of Rs 15,000 per month as against the current Rs 8,000. Other demands include release of pending National Health Mission (NHM) incentives, and better service and retirement benefits.
The D.K. Shivakumar-led Congress government in Karnataka has faced criticism for neglecting the demands of ASHA workers even as the chief minister tours Japan. Shivakumar did put out a post of himself on a video call with ASHA workers from aboard a bullet train in Japan, but it did not quell the criticism of the government for failing to provide the bare minimum sought by these crucial enablers of the public health system.
ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸದಾ ನಮ್ಮ ಸರ್ಕಾರವಿದೆ
ಇಂದು ಜಪಾನ್ ಪ್ರವಾಸದ ನಡುವೆಯೇ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಸಂಘದ ಪದಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ವಿಡಿಯೋ ಕರೆ ಮೂಲಕ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ, ಅವರ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳ ಕುರಿತು ಮುಂಬರುವ ವಿಧಾನಸಭೆ ಅಧಿವೇಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ, ಹಣಕಾಸು ಇಲಾಖೆಯ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಮಾಲೋಚಿಸಿ ಸೂಕ್ತ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳುವುದಾಗಿ ಭರವಸೆ… pic.twitter.com/2K0xMtAxAz
— DK Shivakumar (@DKShivakumar) November 24, 2026
The protests have fuelled criticism by the Opposition, which says that the situation proves the precarious financial position the state finds itself in. “What the ASHA workers are asking for is not a ‘necklace’, sir, but fair pay for the hard work they do. This government’s neglect of the ASHA workers’ struggle is utterly condemnable. For the eighth day, they have continued their round-the-clock sit-in with their children, undeterred by the cold, rain or wind,” Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka wrote in a post on X.
He added that the government’s response—that it would consider the demands in December during the Winter Session—was the “height of absurdity and irresponsibility”. He added that the ASHA workers were not begging, but fighting for their rights.
“The government must stop testing the patience of the ASHA workers who have taken to the streets for justice, intervene immediately, meet their demands and put an end to this inhumane sit-in. We fully support the ASHA workers’ just struggle, and they remain firm in their resolve not to end their protest,” he added.
Narendraswamy has since expressed regret over his comment, saying they were made in the heat of the moment, and that he has withdrawn it.
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)
